source.findings: The reviewed lefamulin table establishes oral/IV doses and safety context. Reviewed chapter-end administration, storage, laboratory and counseling tables do not establish the complete original food interval/exposure rationale, water quantity, whole-tablet/no-crushing/dividing policy, missed-dose interval or oral duration rule. Generic antibiotic food advice is not applied to lefamulin; food/manipulation guidance for other antibiotics is not borrowed. QT context alone does not establish food/crushing pharmacokinetics.

lesson.title: Build the Dose Around Fasting, Water, and Time
lesson.summary: Oral lefamulin must be taken at least one hour before a meal or two hours after a meal, swallowed whole with 6 to 8 ounces of water, and never crushed or divided. Missed doses follow an eight-hour rule.
lesson.application: Write the actual meal, dose, sleep, other medication, and missed-dose schedule before selecting outpatient oral therapy.

lesson.heading: Food timing protects exposure
lesson.body: Take each dose at least one hour before a meal or two hours afterward. Do not copy with-food counseling from another antibiotic.

lesson.heading: The tablet remains whole
lesson.body: Swallow the blue 600 mg tablet whole with 6 to 8 ounces of water. A patient who cannot swallow it should use another feasible plan rather than crush it.

lesson.heading: Eight hours determines a missed dose
lesson.body: Take a missed dose when at least eight hours remain before the next scheduled dose. If fewer than eight hours remain, skip it and resume the schedule.

lesson.heading: A short course can still be operationally difficult
lesson.body: Twice-daily fasting windows, whole-tablet swallowing, interactions, cost, and access can defeat adherence. Test the schedule with the patient before discharge.

keyPoints: Dose at least one hour before or two hours after food.
Swallow whole with 6 to 8 ounces of water.
Never crush or divide the tablet.

Take the missed tablet with a meal
Restart the five-day count
check.rationale: The label directs skipping the missed dose when fewer than eight hours remain.
